Plumber Summer Hill: Village Houses, Art Deco Flats and Old Sewers

A small village with a long plumbing history.

Inner West Sydney Plumbers covers Summer Hill and Lewisham. Summer Hill keeps its village feel, with Federation and Victorian houses, red brick flats from between the wars and a small shopping centre near the station. Most homes here are more than eighty years old, and so is much of the pipework under them.

Why Summer Hill plumbing is a little different

Summer Hill has more than a hundred heritage listed properties for a suburb of its size, and much of the north of the suburb grew from one 1878 estate subdivision. Small lots, shared walls and old flats all affect how a plumber gets to the pipes and what they find there.

Victorian and Federation houses

Houses built between the 1880s and 1920s usually have a clay sewer running under a narrow side path, often close to the neighbour's line. Roots and cracked joints are common.

Inter-war flats

North Summer Hill has two and three storey Art Deco flat buildings. Their shared cast iron stacks and old risers carry the waste of every unit, so one block can affect several homes.

Village shops

The cafes and shops near the station rely on kitchen drains and hot water that keep working through a busy morning. We book planned work before opening or after close.

A heritage sewer next door

The old Lewisham sewage aqueduct, a State listed structure, crosses into Summer Hill. It is a reminder that this part of Sydney was sewered early, and many private lines are of the same age.

Plumbing in Summer Hill and Lewisham

A plumber Summer Hill residents call is usually dealing with one of four jobs: a blocked sewer, a hot water system that has stopped, a leak in an old wall, or a shared pipe in a block of flats. These are the jobs we do most across Summer Hill and Lewisham.

Blocked drains

Clearing roots and debris from old clay lines with high pressure water, then a camera check so you know whether the line needs repair. Our blocked drain page explains each method.

Hot water

Repairs and replacements for gas and electric systems, including tight laundries and flats where the unit sits in a cupboard or on a balcony.

Leaks in old walls

Old copper joints inside brick walls can leak for months before damp shows. We find the source before any wall is opened.

Flats and strata

Blocked stacks, leaking risers and water between floors in inter-war flats, with a written report for the strata manager when the pipe is common property.

Signs your Summer Hill drains need attention

Old clay drains in Summer Hill rarely fail all at once. They give warning signs first, and catching them early usually means a smaller repair. If you notice any of these, it is worth booking a check before the line blocks completely.

  • Gurgling from the toilet or shower when the washing machine empties
  • Water rising in the outdoor gully after rain or a long shower
  • A sewage smell near the side path or in the laundry
  • Toilets that flush slowly or need a second flush
  • Damp, sunken ground along the line of the sewer
  • The same drain blocking again within a few months

House or inter-war flat: who looks after which pipe

In a Summer Hill house you own every pipe on your lot. In a block of flats, responsibility is split between you and the owners corporation, and knowing which pipe is which saves an argument about the bill. This is the usual split.

General guide only. Your strata plan and by-laws decide each case.

Tap, toilet and showerOwnerOwner, inside the unit

What a Summer Hill plumber costs

We price every Summer Hill job before work starts. The age of the pipe, how tight the access is down a narrow side path, and whether the work affects other units in a building are what change the price most.

For published rates, read our Inner West plumber pricing guide.

  1. Age of the pipeOld clay and galvanised pipe often needs repair rather than a simple clear.
  2. AccessNarrow side paths and small lots can mean hand digging.
  3. Shared pipesWork on common property in flats needs strata approval.
  4. The part neededHot water units for tight spaces are priced by size and type.
  5. TimingNight and weekend callouts cost more than a weekday booking.

Summer Hill plumbing questions

What Summer Hill and Lewisham home owners ask us. Anything else, call 0412 395 426.

Do you cover Lewisham as well as Summer Hill?

Yes. Summer Hill and Lewisham are both within our regular area, along with Ashfield, Haberfield, Petersham and Dulwich Hill. Call 0412 395 426 and we will give you an arrival time before you book anything.

My flat's bathroom leaks into the unit below. Who do I call?

Call us and tell your strata manager. We find where the water is coming from, whether a pipe, a fitting or failed waterproofing, and send a written report so the owner or the owners corporation can arrange the right repair.

Can you reach a sewer that runs down a narrow side path?

Usually, yes. Most clearing and camera work is done from the gully or an inspection opening. If a section needs repair, we use compact equipment or dig by hand so neighbours' paths and fences are not disturbed.

Do you work on heritage houses in Summer Hill?

Yes. Many Summer Hill homes are in a heritage conservation area. We keep new pipework out of sight where we can, and match downpipes and visible fittings to the house when the work is on the street side.

How do I know if my hot water system is worth repairing?

If the tank is under about ten years old and the fault is a part such as a thermostat or valve, repair usually makes sense. A leaking tank cannot be repaired and needs replacing. We tell you which applies before you decide.

Can you fix plumbing for a cafe in the Summer Hill village?

Yes. We clear kitchen drains, repair hot water and fix toilets for cafes and shops in the village, and book planned work before opening or after close so trading is not interrupted.

Are your Summer Hill plumbers licensed and insured?

Yes. Every plumber we send holds an NSW plumbing licence, and the business holds NSW contractor licence 306733C with full insurance. You can check any trade licence on the Service NSW website.
